purpose: Editorial review of the 12 legacy mixed routes. This file does not alter public map data.
editorialRule: A diaspora can have several migration histories. Historical forced movement and modern voluntary/refugee movement must be separate records.

records.legacyName: Afro-Bahamian ← Liberated Africans from intercepted slave ships after 1807

proposedMovements.note: These people were captives on illegal slave ships and were resettled after interception. The movement is not an ongoing mixed route; its terminal date requires direct review of the cited source.

legacySources: Michael Craton, 'Islanders in the Stream: A History of the Bahamian People' (1992)

records.legacyName: Afro-Bahamian ← West and Central Africa (via American Loyalist migration)

proposedMovements.note: The movement concerns enslaved Africans carried by British Loyalists. The end year must be established from the cited historical work rather than inherited from the present-day community.

legacySources: Michael Craton, 'Islanders in the Stream: A History of the Bahamian People' (1992)

records.legacyName: East African-descended Emiratis and African migrant workers ← East Africa (historical, via Indian Ocean/Gulf trade)

proposedMovements.note: Historical enslavement must be a bounded route. The start date and exact jurisdictions require stronger historical sourcing; 1963 is retained only as the abolition date stated in the existing fiche.

legacySources: Human Rights Watch, reporting on the kafala system in Gulf states
Historical record of the 1963 Trucial States abolition of slavery

proposedMovements.note: Contemporary labour migration is distinct from historical enslavement. Exploitative employment conditions do not automatically turn the migration route itself into historical slavery.

legacySources: Human Rights Watch, reporting on the kafala system in Gulf states
Historical record of the 1963 Trucial States abolition of slavery

records.legacyName: Afro-French (Hexagone) ← Maghreb migration with sub-Saharan heritage

proposedMovements.note: The existing route description concerns modern migration, not a single forced-and-voluntary movement. Exact start date and the phrase 'sub-Saharan heritage' require source-by-source review.

records.legacyName: Somali and Eritrean Norwegian ← Somalia (post-1991 civil war)

proposedMovements.note: This route is primarily refugee migration and related family reunification, not a simultaneous forced/voluntary route.

legacySources: Statistics Norway (SSB), population by country background

records.legacyName: Afro-Omani (Zanzibar-linked) ← Zanzibar and the East African coast (via centuries of Omani

proposedMovements.note: The legacy text combines Omani political rule, trade, intermarriage and slavery. These cannot be represented as one route until each movement is sourced separately.
The post-revolution movement to Oman is a distinct refugee/return movement, not a continuation of centuries of trade or enslavement. Its end year requires research.

legacySources: Historical records of the Sultanate of Zanzibar (1698–1964)
1970 Omani royal decree abolishing slavery

records.legacyName: Afro-Qatari and African migrant workers ← East African coast (historical, via pearling economy)

proposedMovements.note: Historical enslaved labour in the pearling economy is a bounded forced movement. The start date requires stronger historical sourcing; 1952 is retained only as the abolition date stated in the existing fiche.

legacySources: Amnesty International and Human Rights Watch reporting on Qatar's kafala system and 2022 World Cup labor conditions
Historical record of Qatar's 1952 abolition of slavery

records.legacyName: Afro-Qatari and African migrant workers ← Kenya, Uganda, Nigeria, Ghana (contemporary labor migration)

proposedMovements.note: Modern labour migration is a separate route from historical enslavement. Coercive labour conditions must be documented in the route narrative but do not justify merging both histories into one mixed route.

proposedMovements.note: The described Yoruba 'recaptives' and earlier enslaved populations are historical forced movements. Indian indenture mentioned in the fiche is a separate population history and must not make this African route mixed.
